title: Henselian lift of a pointed universal residual cover
statement: Let $B$ be a Noetherian commutative ring and $J\subseteq B$ an ideal with $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ nonempty connected. Fix a geometric point $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $(E,JE)=(B^h,JB^h)$ be the pair henselization [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. Then $E$ is Noetherian with nonempty connected spectrum and $E/JE=B/J$. Reduction gives an equivalence between the small cofinal pointed connected finite etale Galois cover systems of $\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ [lem-sfb-pointed-finite-etale-limit-cover], including pointed morphisms and group actions. Write the former as $\operatorname{Spec}C_\lambda$, and set $H=\varinjlim_\lambda C_\lambda$. Each $C_\lambda$ is Noetherian, $(C_\lambda,JC_\lambda)$ and $(H,JH)$ are henselian pairs [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and their marked ideals are contained in their Jacobson radicals (the intersections of their maximal ideals). Each $\operatorname{Spec}C_\lambda$ is nonempty connected, and the maps $B\to E$, $B\to C_\lambda$ and $B\to H$ are ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]; $\operatorname{Spec}H$ is the pointed universal cover of $\operatorname{Spec}E$. Moreover $H/JH=\varinjlim_\lambda C_\lambda/JC_\lambda$, and its spectrum is exactly the pointed universal finite-etale limit of $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$, a nonempty connected pro-etale covering [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $J=0$ the canonical map $B\to E$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply pair_henselization to transfer henselianity to the given colimit by its unique under-category isomorphism. Apply pair_henselization_flat_quotients at n=1 for the canonical residual bijection and pair_henselization_noetherian_completion for Noetherianity. The defining essentially-small filtered etale diagram is an ind presentation; transport along ULift equivalences gives IndEtaleAcrossUniverses.

Use the quotient ring isomorphism to transfer connectedness of Spec(B/J) to Spec(E/JE). An idempotent of E reduces to zero or one; if it reduces to zero, its complement is a unit because JE lies in the Jacobson radical, and the idempotent vanishes. Apply the same argument to the complement for reduction one. The quotient map gives nonemptiness. This proves connectedness of Spec E.

Apply [thm-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting] with $(A,I)=(E,JE)$ and $Y=S=\operatorname{Spec}E$. The identity $Y\to S$ is proper by [def-weil-proper-morphism]: every base change is the identity and hence closed, its diagonal is the identity closed immersion, and its affine ring maps are generated by the empty set. Thus reduction is fully faithful and essentially surjective on finite etale covers, and its clause (d) gives the lifting of group actions. This is precisely the affine equivalence of the source.

proof.text: A category equivalence preserves connected objects. The pullback fiber isomorphism transports the transitive automorphism action on every Galois object, so pullback induces a fully faithful and essentially surjective functor on pointed Galois objects. Compose with the existing small-model equivalences to obtain the required equivalence of Index categories. Its unit isomorphism supplies finite_iso and its pointed-morphism equation supplies finite_point. Full faithfulness identifies automorphism groups.

proof.text: Use the existing small cofiltered UniversalCover.Index directly, without introducing a normal-subgroup model. The finite covers over the affine scheme Spec E are affine. Take their global sections with structure maps transported through GammaSpecIso to construct the diagram in Under E. Global sections carry the existing limit cone to a colimit cocone, and the affine isoSpec comparisons give all stage and universal projection equations. Finite E-algebras are Noetherian.

proof.text: The existing index category is cofiltered, hence the opposite ring diagram is filtered. Every element of the colimit is represented by a stage element. Map its monic integral equation from that finite stage to the colimit. Thus the colimit algebra is integral over E, and henselianRing_of_isIntegral gives the colimit henselian pair. Apply the same integral-extension theorem to each finite stage.
Use HenselianRing.jac for E, each finite stage, and the integral colimit; this is exactly containment of the marked ideal in the Jacobson radical.

source.place: Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), proof of (3) implies (1), maximal-ideal argument

proof.text: An etale map belongs to the ind closure by the one-object presentation. The existing filtered diagram of stage rings is itself an ind presentation of E to H. Composition in MorphismProperty.ind with the henselization map proves B to each stage and B to H are ind-etale. Transport the maps through the two canonical ULift isomorphisms for the across-universes predicate.

Construct the quotient colimit by lifting each test cocone to rings using the canonical quotient maps. The ring-colimit desc kills the extended marked ideal, since it kills the base ideal at any stage; quotient lift gives the unique map. Each residual stage is the actual pullback along the residual immersion, by the quotient pushout square. Combine its canonical pullback isomorphism with finite_iso to obtain the residual diagram isomorphism. Spec preserves the opposite quotient colimit, and whiskering the residual universal-cover limit by the pointed equivalence gives another limit of that diagram. The unique comparison isomorphism gives the specified residual stage equations. Those equations give the base equation and, using finite_point, the marked point equation. Connectedness, weak etaleness and surjectivity of the existing residual universal cover transfer along this isomorphism; affineness and surjectivity give the singleton proetale covering.

proof.text: For J=0, use the canonical residual quotient bijection from step 1. The quotient maps modulo the zero ideal are injective and surjective, so this bijection gives injectivity and surjectivity of B to E directly.
